name: Shortest delivery window for each parcel
brief:
A courier offers delivery windows `[start, end]`, each covering the time from `start` up to but not including `end`. For each time in `parcels`, return the length `end - start` of the shortest window that covers it, or `-1` when no window does. The answers follow the order of `parcels`.

Write `shortest_windows(windows, parcels)`.

Example. For `windows = [[0, 10], [4, 6], [8, 20]]` and `parcels = [5, 9, 20]`, time 5 sits in `[4, 6]` of length 2, time 9 is best served by `[0, 10]` of length 10, and nothing covers 20. The answer is `[2, 10, -1]`.
constraints: $0 \le n, q \le 100{,}000$ windows and parcels, with $\text{start} < \text{end}$, all integers of size at most $10^9$.
$O((n + q) \log n)$ time is the target. Checking every window for every parcel is too slow.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Answer the parcels in time order, not input order. Feed the windows, sorted by start, into a heap keyed by length, and pop any window at the top whose end is at or before the current time.

examples.note: Time 9 sits in windows of length 10 and 12, and window ends are not covered.
With no windows, no parcel is covered.
Time 3 is where `[1, 3]` ends, so only `[1, 5]` covers it. The answers keep the order of `parcels`.

tests.call: (lambda r: (sum(r), r.count(-1), r[::10000]))(shortest_windows([[j, j + 1 + (j * 7919) % 1000] for j in range(0, 300000, 3)], [(i * 7) % 310000 for i in range(100000)]))
(lambda r: (sum(r), r.count(-1), r[::10000]))(shortest_windows([[j * 4, j * 4 + 2 + j % 5] for j in range(100000)], [(i * 13) % 400010 for i in range(100000)]))

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Sorting the parcels by time lets each window enter the heap once, as its start passes, and leave once, after its end.
Answering parcels in input order is the trap: the sweep needs times in increasing order, so sort with the index and write each answer back to its place.
Sorting both lists and the heap work give $O((n + q) \log n)$ time and $O(n + q)$ space.
